summary.text: Natalie Fleming, an Independent, rancher's daughter and mother of four, lost the November 3, 2026 election for the U.S. Senate seat in Idaho to Jim Risch.
She worked in the technology industry, returned to school to earn a Boise State degree in 2024, and has written two books.

paragraphs.text: Fleming was born in Portland, Oregon, and describes herself as a rancher's daughter from Idaho's high desert.
She graduated from Moscow High School, and her campaign website says she attended junior high and high school in Moscow.
Her website says she went to work in technology straight out of high school, first at WordPerfect and then at Novell.

By her own account, she returned to Idaho in 2002 as a single mother and worked in software while caring for family members with special needs; her website says she raised her four children in the Treasure Valley.
Fleming returned to school during COVID and earned a bachelor's degree from Boise State University in 2024.
She describes her degrees as in Information Technology Management and Supply Chain Management, with a minor in Cybersecurity.
Ballotpedia lists her career experience as working as an information technology professional.
Fleming has written two books, one on defying hate propaganda and one on restoring the water cycle.
During the campaign, she focused on limits on surveillance and AI, housing affordability and restoring the water cycle.
She received 7.0% of the vote to Jim Risch's 56.5%, according to unofficial results reported by NBC News.
